scene: Inferno XIX — the third bolgia, inverted simoniacs and Nicholas III
story: Dante and Virgil look down into the third bolgia, a rocky floor pierced by round holes.
The simoniacs are thrust head-first into these holes; their exposed feet and legs writhe under flickering flames.
One pair of feet kicks harder than the rest; Virgil carries Dante down the slope to investigate.
Dante speaks to the inverted soul, who mistakes him for Boniface VIII, whom he expects to arrive later.
The speaker is Pope Nicholas III. His mistaken expectation reveals a prediction and his own temporal viewpoint, not the visitor's identity.
Dante condemns the sale of sacred offices. Virgil approves his words and carries him back up toward the next crossing.
The soul remains inverted: interrogation reveals identity without reorienting or releasing him.
